front: Worked: PV source circuit, 10 modules in series, Isc = 9.5 A — circuit current and conductor ampacity
back:
Max circuit current = 125 % × Isc = 11.9 A (690.8(A)(1))
Conductor ampacity ≥ 125 % × that = 14.8 A before corrections (690.8(B)(1)) — i.e., 156 % of Isc
OR ampacity ≥ 11.9 A after temperature/conduit-fill corrections — use the larger result (690.8(B)(2))
Series string: current stays 9.5 A, voltage adds

front: Worked: max PV system voltage for 12 modules in series, Voc = 45 V, lowest expected ambient −20 °C
back:
Table 690.7(A) factor at −16 to −20 °C ≈ 1.18 (when the module temperature coefficient isn't given)
12 × 45 × 1.18 = 637 V dc
One- and two-family dwellings: ≤ 600 V (690.7) — this fails; 11 modules = 584 V ✔ or use the module's own coefficient
Other buildings: ≤ 1000 V; up to 1500 V only where not on or in buildings
note: Confirm the Table 690.7(A) factor for −16 to −20 °C (1.18) and the 600 V dwelling limit wording in 2020 690.7. Method is settled.

front: Worked: 120 % rule — 200 A busbar, 200 A main, adding a PV breaker
back:
Allowed: main + inverter OCPD ≤ 120 % × busbar = 240 A
240 − 200 = 40 A max PV breaker, located at the opposite end from the main (705.12(B)(3)(2))
Inverter output 7.6 kW at 240 V = 31.7 A → 125 % = 39.6 A → 40 A breaker ✔ fits exactly
Alternative: sum of all breakers excluding main ≤ busbar rating (705.12(B)(3)(3))

front: Worked: EV charger rated 48 A continuous — branch circuit
back:
EVSE is continuous (625.41): 48 × 1.25 = 60 A → 60 A breaker, 6 AWG Cu 75 °C (65 A)
A 40 A EVSE → 50 A circuit; 32 A → 40 A
2020 625.42: load management systems may set the max to the managed value

Receptacles: ≥ 6 ft from the inside wall; at least one general-purpose receptacle 6–20 ft (680.22(A)); GFCI for 15/20 A 125 V receptacles within 20 ft
Pump motor: GFCI on 15/20 A 125–250 V 1φ outlets (680.21(C))
Wet-niche luminaires: top of the lens ≥ 18 in below the normal water level (680.23(A)(5))
Switches: ≥ 5 ft horizontally from the inside wall unless separated by a barrier (680.22(C))

front: Worked: receptacles at a patient bed location — general care vs critical care
back:
Category 2 (general care): ≥ 8 receptacles, at least one from the normal system and one from the critical branch, or from 2 critical branch transfer switches (517.18(B))
Category 1 (critical care): ≥ 14 receptacles, at least one normal + one critical branch (517.19(B)(1))
All hospital-grade, listed, identified

front: Transfer times and testing — worked recall
back:
Emergency (700): power available within 10 s (700.12); monthly testing/maintenance records (700.3)
Legally required standby (701): within 60 s (701.12)
Optional standby (702): no time limit; load calc per 702.4
Emergency wiring kept separate from other wiring (700.10(B))

front: Worked: Class I Div 1 conduit seals — where within what distance?
back:
Seal within 18 in of each enclosure containing arcing/sparking parts, or any conductor splice/terminal (501.15(A)(1))
Seal where conduit leaves the Div 1 area — within 10 ft of the boundary, no unions/couplings/boxes between the seal and the boundary (501.15(A)(4))
Conduit 2 in and larger entering enclosures with splices/taps: seal within 18 in (501.15(A)(1)(2))
Threaded RMC/IMC with ≥ 5 threads engaged (500.8(E))

Major repair garage, unventilated: Class I Div 2 up to 18 in above floor (511.3(C)); ventilated (4 ACH or 1 cfm/ft²) → unclassified
Pits without ventilation: Div 1
Minor repair, no fuel work: unclassified
GFCI on 125 V 15/20 A receptacles for tools, diagnostics, etc. (511.12)

Equipotential plane in concrete floors of livestock confinement areas and outdoor concrete areas where livestock stand and energized equipment is nearby (547.10)
GFCI: all 125 V 15/20 A general-purpose receptacles in areas with equipotential planes, outdoors, damp/wet locations, dirt confinement areas (547.5(G))
Site-isolating device at the distribution point (547.9)
Corrosion-resistant wiring methods; dust-tight boxes
